Messages.Author: Martin Filion
Messages.Body:
Hi!
My friends and I banned Monocle of Clarity in our games. Why? Because
of that 2 combined questions...

- First Question: Will you answer yes at the question I'll ask you in my
next Uptap phase...

If he says no, which means he'll answer no at my next question...

- Second Question: Will your vampires try to block my vampires when
they'll attempt to bleed you, and that, for the
remainder of the game and each games we'll do
together forever?

If he says yes, which means he'll answer yes at my next question...

- Second Question: Will your vampires will not try to block my vampires
when they'll attempt to bleed you, and that, for the
remainder of the game and each games we'll do together
forever?

That's it... And after that, you can bleed this player as long as
you want at each game you play with him...

Martin Filion
Montreal, Qb (Canada)

There was also an article by Tom that said that the only thing you
cannot ask is "will you answer yes or no to my next question". The
meaning of that is that MofC does not bind your opponent to any future
questions.

You could ask "Dou you block if I bleed you?", and make your prey
either block every time the remainder of the game or let the bleed go
through every time. And all that just because you "forgot" to say
"next time". This could be handy if you end up with a huge weapon and
know for sure that your prey must block. :)

Messages.Author: K R Maxson
Messages.Body:

Marko Puumalainen <ma...@beta.hut.fi> wrote:
>There was also an article by Tom that said that the only thing you

>questions.
>You could ask "Dou you block if I bleed you?", and make your prey
>either block every time the remainder of the game or let the bleed go
>through every time. And all that just because you "forgot" to say
>"next time". This could be handy if you end up with a huge weapon and
>know for sure that your prey must block. :)

All this fuss over the Monocle of Clarity is kind of stupid. It should be
obvious that just because an answer of "yes" or "no" is possible does NOT make
a question a "yes or no" question. For example:

Monocle Asshole: Will you have 11 pool for the remainder of the game?
Answer yes or no, please.

What can the poor target say? A yes or no question is one with ONLY two
possible answers: yes, you got it -- "yes" or "no."

Monocle Asshole: For the remainder of the game, when I bleed you, will
you block?

Innocent Target: That is not a "yes or no" question. Fuck off.

Don't munchkinize a game that is, by some miracle, moderately well balanced!
They are too few and far between.

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
k...@cerl.uiuc.edu (K R Maxson) writes:

>In article <marko.7...@snakemail.hut.fi>,

>All this fuss over the Monocle of Clarity is kind of stupid. It should be
>obvious that just because an answer of "yes" or "no" is possible does NOT make
>a question a "yes or no" question. For example:

All questions worded as "Will you X" are yes/no questions.

> Monocle /Explicative: Will you have 11 pool for the remainder of the game?

> Answer yes or no, please.

>What can the poor target say? A yes or no question is one with ONLY two
>possible answers: yes, you got it -- "yes" or "no."

What other answer is there to this question?
The only valid answer is "no", as the game cannot end with the target
never having changed from 11 pool.
This is a yes/no question.
I defy anyone to present an answer that is not affiramtive nor negative
("maybe" is obviously not allowed) which is a valid answer to this question.

> Monocle /Explicative: For the remainder of the game, when I bleed you, will
> you block?

> Innocent Target: That is not a "yes or no" question. /Explicative off.
Innocent target is mistaken. It is a yes/no question. "Fruit", "Two"
and "Yesterday" simply don't cut it as answers to this question. Only
"Yes" or "No" will do (or other forms of "Affirmative" and "Negative" :-).

The best reply is "no." You then only have to not block once, and will have
fulfilled your obligation to NOT(block whenever bled).

>Don't munchkinize a game that is, by some miracle, moderately well balanced!
>They are too few and far between.

If one can't grasp a concept as simple as a yes/no question, one shouldn't
play Jyhad.

Agreed that the above questions are out of place. However, there
are some perfectly legitimate questions that are quite "powerful",
if a "yes or no" answer is enforced:

Will you throw at least as many "for" votes as "against"
votes in the next vote to be called (by anybody)?

Answer:
yes - he, he, now you can't vote against this one (of mine)
no - so you have to vote against the next vote, and I
can see that it'll be yours

Will you play any Manuevers in the next combat round you
fight?
(So I choose range, you shut up.)

>
>>>Don't munchkinize a game that is, by some miracle, moderately well balanced!
>>>They are too few and far between.

Unfortunately, the game is excessively buggy. (What's happening
with Blood Rage?)
